newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc to test US$1,400, copper to seek $2,600.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc to test US$1,400, copper to seek $2,600.

text.p: Far East metal dealers said London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices are tipped to test the key US$1,400 level later on Friday while copper is also expected to try to regain a toehold above $2,600 a tonne.
"Zinc is going to see $1,400 today. If it breaks that level, then $1,410 and $1,420 will come easily," a dealer for a metal firm in Singapore said.
"Zinc is still pretty strong. It's definitely going to try $1,400. There's very good support for the metal at $1,380," another dealer added.
Zinc powered to a 4-3/4-year high on the LME on Thursday, with prices coming close to the psychological $1,400 barrier.
LME brokers Brandeis said zinc had a strong close on the charts on Thursday with "a test of $1,400 looking likely in the short term."
"The initial target is $1,400 and then $1,435," broker Rudolf Wolff said in its daily report.
But brokers Macquarie cautioned that "some retracement is expected unless consumer interest adds its weight behind this uptrend."
Three-month zinc was quoted by the trade at 0230 GMT at around $1,392/96, little changed from the late quote on the LME on Thursday of $1,393/95 a tonne.
Copper prices are poised to make another stab at the elusive $2,600 mark on the LME, dealers said.
"Copper will take another try at $2,600," one dealer said.
"It should move higher by another $50. If you follow the big boys, the trend should be higher," another trader said.
Three-month copper was quoted by regional dealers firmer at about $2,585/90 a tonne against the late quote on the LME on Thursday of $2,582/85.

"The upside still remains the favoured direction as we look for further signs of strength," Rudolf Wolff said, adding though that if copper fails to break higher as the weekend approaches "increased profit-taking may emerge."
Brandeis and Macquarie, however, feel the flagship metal will be range-bound for the short-term.
"We see copper within the recent range for the short term with underlying support seemingly intact," Macquarie said.
